title: Crying Is a Newborn's Main Language
hook: Crying is how a newborn communicates every need — and a lot of crying in the first months is normal, peaking around six weeks and easing after that.
key_points: Common causes: hunger, a dirty diaper, tiredness, overstimulation, or just wanting to be held.
Crying often peaks at around 6 weeks of age, then gradually decreases — a normal developmental pattern.
Responding to cries does not 'spoil' a young baby; it builds trust and security.
Never shake a baby. If you feel overwhelmed, put the baby down safely and take a break.
content_html: In the early weeks, crying is a newborn's entire vocabulary. It's the only way they have to tell you they're hungry, tired, wet, too stimulated, or simply in need of contact. Working through that short checklist — feed, change, calm the environment, hold — resolves most episodes.
extra_html: It also helps to know that a lot of crying is developmentally normal: for many babies it builds to a peak around six weeks of age, then gradually settles. Responding to your baby's cries doesn't spoil them — at this age it builds the security and trust that healthy development rests on. One firm safety rule: never shake a baby, which can cause severe brain injury. If the crying ever leaves you feeling at the end of your rope, it is safe and sensible to put the baby down in their crib and step away for a few minutes to collect yourself. This is general information; persistent or unusual crying is worth raising with your health visitor or pediatrician.

related.title: Always Put a Baby to Sleep on Their Back
related.hook: Placing healthy babies on their back for every sleep — naps and night — is the single most effective step to reduce the risk of sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS).

flashcards.prompt: What are common reasons a newborn cries?
flashcards.back_html: Hunger, a dirty diaper, tiredness, overstimulation, or simply wanting to be held — crying is how a newborn signals every need.

flashcards.prompt: Does responding quickly to a young baby's cries spoil them?

choices.text: No — responding builds trust and security
Yes, it teaches them to cry more on purpose
Yes, babies should learn to self-soothe from birth

flashcards.explanation_html: You can't spoil a newborn by responding. Comforting cries builds a secure attachment; deliberate "manipulation" isn't yet within a newborn's ability.

flashcards.prompt: What should you do if a crying baby leaves you feeling overwhelmed?

choices.text: Put the baby down somewhere safe and take a short break
Shake the baby gently to startle them quiet
Leave the house and come back later

flashcards.explanation_html: Never shake a baby — it can cause serious brain injury. Placing the baby safely in a crib while you step away to calm down is the safe choice.
